top_story_title: CISA adds HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Router command injection to the KEV catalog - root via a crafted salt minion ID
top_story_summary: CISA added CVE-2026-103406 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-25. The flaw is an OS command injection in Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router: a remote attacker can execute arbitrary commands as root by supplying a specially crafted salt minion ID. The federal remediation due date is 2026-11-28, which is three days out - treat that as the signal for how fast this is being exploited.
top_actions: Inventory every Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router and record the running version; the Conductor is the priority asset because it controls the routers.
Check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and the mitigation for CVE-2026-103406, then patch or mitigate the Conductor first and the routers after, inside an emergency change.
Remove the Conductor's management and Salt channel from any internet-facing or untrusted interface; restrict to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network with an explicit ACL.

Treat any reachable Conductor as potentially compromised: rotate local admin credentials, API keys, certificates and router onboarding secrets after patching, because root access survives an upgrade otherwise.

Hunt for persistence on Conductor and routers - unexpected local accounts, new or modified salt states and minion configuration, unexplained root shell history, new outbound connections and changed static routes or tunnels.
executive_summary: CISA added CVE-2026-103406 in HPE Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router to the KEV catalog on 2026-11-25 with a 2026-11-28 due date: remote root via a crafted salt minion ID, and the Conductor is the management plane for a router fleet.

A China-linked group chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia flaw in AI-assisted attacks to root Palo Alto Networks firewalls across 25 servers; Palo Alto Networks has shipped patches, so confirm your PAN-OS build against the vendor advisory.

GreyNoise reports 24 Check Point Security Management servers compromised across 22 organisations using AI-driven offensive tooling - a management-platform compromise, so rotate managed-gateway credentials, not just the server's own.

Upstream component flaws dominate the vendor advisories: Cisco is assessing Node.js (including KEV-listed Brotli CVE-2026-111497), nginx and PHP (phpAfterShell CVE-2026-126714), and Palo Alto Networks has opened a critical portfolio-status bulletin for the nginx CVEs.
No collected source states a fixed release for the Juniper KEV entry or for Fragnesia - check the vendor advisory before scheduling any change, and do not act on a version number from a news report.
Webworm is recompiling SoftEther VPN from source to strip detection artifacts, so inventory-based VPN detection will miss it; hunt on egress behaviour instead.
key_actions: **Juniper** — Identify all Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router instances from inventory with their running versions, and patch or mitigate the Conductor before the routers - the controller is the higher-value target.
**Juniper** — Check the vendor advisory for the fixed release and the documented mitigation for CVE-2026-103406; do not act on a version number from a news summary.

**Palo Alto Networks** — Identify your PAN-OS firewalls and their running versions, then confirm each against the Palo Alto Networks advisory's fixed-release table; patch the HA pair secondary first, then fail over.
**Palo Alto Networks** — Treat this as an emergency change for any firewall whose management interface or administrative web access has ever been reachable from the internet.

**Check Point** — Determine whether any Security Management server is reachable from the internet or from untrusted internal zones, and remove that reachability immediately - management servers belong on a dedicated management network.
**Check Point** — Check the Check Point advisories for guidance tied to this campaign and for the fixed release or mitigation if one is published; do not assume a version number from the news report.
**Cisco** — Pull the Cisco advisory and build the affected-product list against your inventory, filtered by model and running version; re-check it, because Cisco says it will be updated.

**Cisco** — Where a product is listed and a fixed release is published, schedule the upgrade; where it is not, check the vendor advisory for the fixed release rather than assuming the Node.js version number maps to a Cisco build.

ai_defenses.solution: AI-powered email threat protection on Check Point's unified email, collaboration and endpoint platform
ai_defenses.what_it_does: Check Point describes AI-powered security that helps prevent phishing, ransomware, account takeover, business email compromise and zero-day attacks, delivered on one platform covering email, collaboration tools and endpoints. The post states the protection extends to the AI assistants that now read and act on email, not only to employees.

headlines.title: CISA KEV addition: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router - CVE-2026-103406
headlines.summary: CISA added a Juniper Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router command-injection flaw to the KEV catalog; a crafted salt minion ID gives a remote attacker root.

headlines.title: Palo Alto Networks Patches Fragnesia Flaw Used to Root Firewalls
headlines.summary: A China-linked group chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia flaw in AI-assisted attacks to gain root on Palo Alto Networks firewalls, hitting 25 servers; patches are out.

headlines.title: Hackers Compromise 24 Check Point Management Servers in Suspected AI-Driven Attack Campaign
headlines.summary: An unknown actor used AI-driven offensive tooling to compromise 24 Check Point Security Management servers across 22 organisations, per GreyNoise.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in Node.js and Brotli Affecting Cisco Products: October 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco's October advisory covers four Node.js flaws in its products, including the KEV-listed Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write that can lead to remote code execution.

headlines.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: Cisco is assessing which of its products ship the nginx releases hit by five critical RCE flaws, fixed upstream in nginx 1.31.9 mainline and 1.30.7 stable.

headlines.title: Vulnerability in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
headlines.summary: A critical PHP remote code execution flaw dubbed phpAfterShell (CVE-2026-126714) is being assessed for impact across Cisco products.
